'''Henricus Grammateus''' (also known as '''Henricus Scriptor''', '''Heinrich Schreyber''' or '''Heinrich Schreiber'''; 1495 – 1525 or 1526<ref>{{cite web |url-status=dead |url=http://www.erfurt-web.de/SchreyberHeinrich |website=erfurt-web.de |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070930184709/http://www.erfurt-web.de/SchreyberHeinrich |archive-date=2007-09-30 |title= Heinrich Schreyber (Henricus Grammateus) }}</ref>) was a [[Germans|German]] [[mathematician]]. He was born in [[Erfurt]]. In 1507 he started to study at the University of Vienna, where he subsequently taught. [[Christoph Rudolff]] was one of his students. From 1514 to 1517 he studied in [[Kraków]] and then returned to Vienna. But when the plague affected Vienna Schreiber left the city and went to [[Nuremberg]].

In 1518, he published details of a new [[musical temperament]],<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.hpschd.nu/index.html?nav/nav-4.html&t/welcome.html&http://www.hpschd.nu/tech/tmp/grammateus.html |title=Temperaments IV: Grammateus |work=Technical Library |publisher=Carey Beebe Harpsichords |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120801151355/http://www.hpschd.nu/index.html?nav/nav-4.html&t/welcome.html&http://www.hpschd.nu/tech/tmp/grammateus.html |archive-date= 1 Aug 2012 }}</ref> which is now named after him, for the [[harpsichord]].  It was a precursor of the [[equal temperament]].

In 1525 Schreiber was back in Vienna, where he is listed as "Examinator", i.e. eligible to work holding exams. 

== Works ==
* ''Algorithmus proportionum una cum monochordi generalis dyatonici compositione'', pub. Volfgangvm De Argentina, Kraków, 1514
* ''Libellus de compositione regularum pro vasorum mensuratione. Deque arte ista tota theoreticae et practicae'', Vienna, 1518
* ''Ayn new Kunstlich Buech'' (''A New Skill Book''), Vienna 1518, Nuremberg 1521 - contains (besides [[Johannes Widmann]]) the earliest-known use of the [[plus and minus signs]] for addition and subtraction<ref>{{cite web |url=http://members.aol.com/jeff570/operation.html |last1=Miller |first1=J. |display-authors=et al. |title=Earliest Uses of Symbols of Operation|website=AOL Hometown |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071014001747/http://members.aol.com/jeff570/operation.html |archive-date= Oct 14, 2007 }}</ref> and is the earliest German text on bookkeeping<ref>{{cite web |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120711034124/http://homepage2.nifty.com/dear-inoue/eng/enggra/eng.html |archive-date=11 Jul 2012 |url=http://homepage2.nifty.com/dear-inoue/eng/enggra/eng.html |last1=Inoue |first1=K. |title=The Neglected Contribution of Grammateus to Bookkeeping History}}</ref>
